title: Symptom record text quotes the UTC instant beside a local zone name
trigger: User in America/Chicago saves a symptom observed 2026-09-11 21:15 local; SymptomEntryEditorView.swift:40 writes observedAt via RevaDate.iso (always 'Z'), so observedAt = 2026-09-12T02:15:00Z, timeZone = America/Chicago; recordText line 66 renders the pair verbatim.
expected: The record body (quoted source for reports, visible record text) states the occurrence in the user's zone or with its real offset, agreeing with the record's list date.
actual: Record text reads 'Occurred at: 2026-09-12T02:15:00Z (America/Chicago)' while record.date is '2026-09-11' (derived in the entry zone, SymptomEntry.swift:101-107). Tests/RevaCoreTests/SymptomEntryTests.swift:77 pins the text and :88 pins the list date, so the mismatch is the current contract. Browser twin apps/web/src/core/symptoms.ts:57 is identical.
impact: Report quotations copy the line verbatim; a reader can attribute the symptom to the wrong day, and the zone suffix invites reading 02:15 as local time. No data loss (observedAt/timeZone stored precisely in symptomEntry).
evidence: sed -n '63,67p;101,107p' apps/ios/Reva/Core/SymptomEntry.swift; sed -n '40p' apps/ios/Reva/Features/Records/SymptomEntryEditorView.swift; sed -n '77p;88p' Tests/RevaCoreTests/SymptomEntryTests.swift; evidence/r1-10-swift-test-root.log lines 104-118 (SymptomEntryTests pass as written). | Independent validation: Core/SymptomEntry.swift:63-67,101-107; browser core/symptoms.ts:57,69-81; SymptomDialog.tsx:64-68 preserves occurrence and zone.
smallestFix: In recordText format observedAt in entry.timeZone with an explicit offset (e.g. '2026-09-11 21:15 (America/Chicago, UTC-05:00)'); mirror in apps/web/src/core/symptoms.ts:57; update the pinned test strings in both clients in the same change.
regressionCheck: SymptomEntryTests: entry 2026-09-12T02:15:00Z / America/Chicago yields record text containing '2026-09-11' and '21:15'; browser symptoms test asserts the identical string.
validatorDisposition: Downgrade: the explicit Z accurately identifies UTC and the parenthesized IANA zone is separately correct. The stored instant and record day are preserved; no contradictory time arithmetic is shown. A friendlier local timestamp plus explicit offset would improve readability.

expected: Quotations end at a line boundary or carry a visible marker so 'Potassium 4.15 mmol/L' cannot become 'Potassium 4.1' and 'No chest pain' cannot become 'No'.
actual: .prefix(1800) cuts at an arbitrary character with no ellipsis or boundary logic. DomainTests.swift:114-117 checks negation only on a 3-line text; FixtureEvidenceTests.swift:136-138 and DomainTests.swift:165 ground excerpts by substring containment, which a mid-token cut still satisfies. impact: Altered dose/unit/negation in the 'Local excerpt' summary and in the pre-visit brief for long pages. Not exercised by the checked-in seed (max joined length 888 chars).
evidence: sed -n '14,16p;161,165p' apps/ios/Reva/Core/ReportEngine.swift; scratchpad port_check.out section 5 (seed max 888); ER-02-02 item 4 requests the Swift demonstration. | Independent validation: Core/ReportEngine.swift:14-15,161-165; browser core/domain.ts:60-61,145-161; evidence/codex-takeover/ProviderContextRepro.swift:110-114; evidence/codex-takeover/provider-context-repro.txt:1,7,15 (compiler/run exit 0; production Swift boundary reproduced).

title: Page tie-break selects the last page for zero-hit or tied multi-page records
trigger: Multi-page record selected by pin (score 1000) or context tag whose pages score equally for the visit focus (seed: 2-page demo-record-tibia-procedure under demo-visit-primary-20260908 scores [1,1]; any pinned scan with zero hits scores all 0).
expected: With no distinguishing hit the citation points at page 1 (the document opening, which is what the fallback excerpt quotes), or the tie rule is explicit and tested.
actual: Sequence.max(by:) replaces the running maximum whenever areInIncreasingOrder(current, candidate) is true; the closure returns lhs.offset < rhs.offset on ties, so a later page always wins and the reference cites the last page. The excerpt is that page's opening lines, so the citation is grounded but points at the least informative page for scans ending in signature/footer pages. Browser twin domain.ts:180-183 uses 'score >= maximum' (same last-page result).
impact: Lower-quality citations for pinned/context documents; no false quotation.
evidence: sed -n '112,118p' apps/ios/Reva/Core/ReportEngine.swift; sed -n '180,183p' apps/web/src/core/domain.ts; port_check.out section 4 ([(1,0),(1,0)] tie under the completed visit); Swift Sequence.max(by:) semantics. | Independent validation: Core/ReportEngine.swift:112-118; browser core/domain.ts:170-198; selected page text and cited page are the same.
smallestFix: Return lhs.offset > rhs.offset on ties (first page wins) in Swift and use 'score > maximum' in the browser; add a comment stating the rule.
regressionCheck: Unit test: 3-page record with zero focus hits and a pin cites page 1; 2-page record with hits only on page 2 still cites page 2.
validatorDisposition: Later-page tie selection is real and deterministic, but no contract establishes that page1 is always more relevant for equal scores. Grounding remains intact. Keep a documented/tested tie policy and a targeted clinical-quality example as an improvement, not a confirmed wrong-source defect.

title: RevaDate.display(time: false) renders the UTC calendar day of instants
trigger: A report generated at 21:30 America/Chicago on 2026-09-11 has createdAt = 2026-09-12T02:30:00Z; ReportView.swift:27 shows RevaDate.display(report.createdAt); RecordingDetailView.swift:27 does the same for recording.createdAt.

impact: Off-by-one day labels for evening activity west of UTC; cosmetic but medical-context sensitive.
evidence: sed -n '203p;225,231p' apps/ios/Reva/Core/Models.swift; sed -n '27p' apps/ios/Reva/Features/Preparation/ReportView.swift; sed -n '27p' apps/ios/Reva/Features/Visits/RecordingDetailView.swift; sed -n '28p' apps/web/src/core/domain.ts. | Independent validation: Core/Models.swift:225-231; Features/Preparation/ReportView.swift:27; browser core/domain.ts:21-29 has the same rule but browser report header passes withTime=true.

title: Per-call formatter allocation in RevaDate and per-access sorting/hashing (unmeasured)
trigger: Any SwiftUI body evaluation that reads store.records or renders the visits list.
expected: Bounded cost per render.
actual: parse allocates up to three formatters per call; AppStore.records sorts on every access with two parse calls per comparison (O(N log N) parses per evaluation); isStale hashes the full record corpus per visit row (VisitsView.swift:45). Asymptotic argument only; no measurement exists, so this is not a defect claim.
impact: Plausible UI latency at the server's 5000-record cap; unknown at demo scale.

validatorDisposition: Allocation/sorting/hash cost is plausible but original report overstates per-record parsing: AppStore.records only parses on equal record dates. title: Startup repair save failure hides a valid loaded snapshot and offers only an unconfirmed demo reset
trigger: LocalRepository.load() succeeds and the loaded snapshot contains the legacy demo title on demo-record-symptom-diary or a non-live booking in queued/calling status; the repair write in AppStore.init (save(sample) at line 70 or mutate at line 75) then fails, e.g. device storage full so state.backup.json/state.json cannot be written.
expected: A successfully loaded valid snapshot stays usable; a repair write failure is reported as a non-blocking error or deferred, and the destructive reset remains an explicit confirmed action.
actual: snapshot is already set at line 60, the repair throw lands in the shared catch at line 86, startupError becomes the raw filesystem error text, and RootView.swift:21-29 replaces the whole UI with an error screen whose only control runs store.resetDemo() with no confirmation (SettingsView.swift:99-102 has one). resetDemo() replaces the active state with the seed (AppStore.swift:136-137); the previous state survives only as the single backup until the next save overwrites it, and no UI restores from backup. Only resetDemo clears startupError (line 138).
impact: Under a plausible device condition (storage exhausted at launch) the user is blocked from valid data and steered to a one-tap action that discards it. Loss requires the user tap and one backup generation remains, hence P2; validators may escalate given the missing confirmation.
evidence: Source proof: AppStore.swift:58-86 (repair mutations 65-82 inside the load do/catch), AppStore.swift:111-116 (mutate throws from repository.save before publishing), RootView.swift:21-29, AppStore.swift:138. Refutation attempts: line 60 runs before either repair so snapshot is non-nil; grep over apps/ios shows startupError is cleared only by resetDemo; RootView gates on nothing else; demo/seed.json already has the new title so the rename repair affects only older installs, but the booking repair applies to any interrupted simulation. Not reproduced at runtime; see evidence request ER-03-5 in reports/track-03.md. | Independent validation: AppStore.swift:59-86,111-115,130-138; Features/Shared/RootView.swift:21-29. evidence/codex-takeover/provider-context-repro.txt (compiler exit0, run exit0); evidence/codex-takeover/ProviderContextRepro.swift:73-108 uses production ReportEngine/AppStore/LocalRepository with synthetic data and a controlled transport double.
smallestFix: Move the two repair mutations out of the load do/catch into their own do/catch that sets errorMessage or notice, reserving startupError for load failures; wrap the RootView reset button in the same confirmation dialog Settings uses.
regressionCheck: OptimizationChecks-style check: save a fixture with a queued non-live booking to a temp LocalRepository, make state.backup.json a directory, construct AppStore(repository:), assert startupError == nil, snapshot != nil, errorMessage/notice set, and the booking still reads queued.
validatorDisposition: Confirmed and now reproduced through the unchanged production AppStore/LocalRepository: a synthetic blocking filesystem entry makes the repair save fail after a valid snapshot loaded, yielding snapshot!=nil and startupError!=nil. RootView then selects its recovery branch by source. No UI/simulator interaction or real user data was used.

title: 409 handling discards the server's X-State-Revision and fetches the whole snapshot to learn the conflict revision
trigger: Any push that returns HTTP 409.
expected: The conflict revision is read from the X-State-Revision header the server already sends on 409 (server/Sources/RevaServer/HTTP.swift:50-53); one round trip.
actual: ServerClient.send maps 409 to ServerFailure.conflict with no payload (line 108). AppStore+Sync.swift:111-125 then issues a second GET /v1/state (up to the 4 MiB snapshot cap, server Models.swift:125) and discards its body to read revision; if that GET fails transiently, serverConflictRevision = nil and the explicit Replace-server control disappears until the push is retried.
impact: Bounded: at most one extra GET of up to 4 MiB per conflict on a developer/demo transfer path plus one extra user retry after a transient failure. No data risk.
evidence: Source proof above. TransportTests.swift:193-210 already sends X-State-Revision: 11 on a 409 and asserts only .conflict. | Independent validation: Core/ServerClient.swift:108; State/AppStore+Sync.swift:111-125; Fable r1-16-client-server covers normal conflict transport.
smallestFix: Give ServerFailure.conflict an Int? parsed from X-State-Revision (mirroring .empty) and use it in the handler; keep the secondary pull only as a fallback when the header is absent.
regressionCheck: Extend the existing transport test to assert the parsed revision; add a StateChecks case where onPush throws .conflict(11) and assert serverConflictRevision == 11 with no pull performed.
validatorDisposition: 409 revision is discarded and a second GET occurs. Current flow preserves local data and makes overwrite explicit. Avoidable response transfer and weaker conflict recovery are a bounded improvement, not demonstrated corruption.
ownerTrack: Captain (shared client transport); header contract already provided by Person 3

title: Push replaces server attachment bytes before the CAS snapshot write while pull refuses the same situation; documented tradeoff, server-side hardening proposed
trigger: Two clients of one owner hold different bytes under the same filename; one pushes and receives 409 from PUT /v1/state after its attachment uploads already replaced the server copies keyed by sha256(filename).
expected: F05 asks whether this is a documented tradeoff or a concrete defect. Assessment: documented tradeoff (README.md:70, docs/architecture.md:202, apps/web/src/core/COMPATIBILITY.md:22) with no first-party producer of same-name/different-bytes: native import names are UUID-prefixed (AddRecordView.swift:264), recordings are recording-<UUID>.m4a (AudioServices.swift:133-134), browser names are uid()-prefixed (ImportDialog.tsx:125) and reva-audio-<id> (RecordingCapture.tsx:113); bundled fixture names are shared but bytes are identical (demo/sources vs iOS Resources: 11/11 SHA-256 equal) and changed in only one commit (eb2ec3a).
actual: Server putAttachment unconditionally replaces bytes independent of the snapshot revision in both stores (LocalFileStore.swift:119-121; PostgresStore.swift:132-133) and the native push uploads before client.push (AppStore+Sync.swift:53-65). The native pull side refuses different bytes under an existing name (LocalRepository.swift:71-77) with a message that tells the user to re-import under a new filename, which is impossible for a bundled fixture name.
impact: Bounded residual risk: if fixture bytes ever diverge between builds or clients, the second pusher silently replaces the server copy referenced by the live snapshot despite its CAS failing, and the other client can no longer pull that owner. Local evidence is never replaced (pull fails closed). The accounts contract (multi-device per user) makes concurrent pushes more likely; forward-looking, not a completed-path defect.
evidence: Source proof above; documentation lines cited; fixture byte comparison performed read-only with shasum. | Independent validation: State/AppStore+Sync.swift:53-65; LocalRepository.swift:67-80; server LocalFileStore.swift:108-121; browser README.md:56 explicitly describes separate operations.
smallestFix: Server: let PUT /v1/attachments/:id refuse to replace existing different bytes unless the client supplies an explicit override (If-Match/expected revision), returning 409 with the current revision. Client: word the pull-conflict message differently for bundled fixture names. Keep fixture bytes pinned via the existing fixture-manifest.json hashes on both clients.
regressionCheck: Server test: upload bytes A, upload bytes B under the same id without override -> 409 and A retained; with override -> replaced. Native: existing StateChecks R2 case stays green.
validatorDisposition: Independent attachment-before-snapshot writes are a documented tradeoff; same-name differing-byte normal UUID imports are uncommon. Keep server immutable/content-addressed attachment hardening as an improvement and avoid claiming all 409s corrupt originals.
ownerTrack: Person 3 (server contract) with Captain for the shared client contract

title: No native content SHA-256 is computed or stored for preserved originals
trigger: The brief's carried-forward product requirement lists preserved originals as bytes, filename, MIME, SHA-256 and pages.
expected: Each preserved original carries a content hash that survives save/reload/sync and can be verified.

title: Native visit ordering compares raw ISO strings, so offset-formatted seed visits and Z-formatted user visits misorder; Summary can show the wrong next visit
trigger: With the bundled demo loaded (seed visit 'demo-visit-primary-20260915' stored as '2026-09-15T09:00:00-05:00' = 14:00Z, apps/ios/Reva/Resources/seed.json:286), add a visit via VisitEditorView for 2026-09-15 08:00 America/Chicago (stored by RevaDate.iso as '2026-09-15T13:00:00Z', VisitEditorView.swift:109, Models.swift:217). Open Summary and the Visits tab.
expected: Visits ordered by instant: the 08:00 visit (13:00Z) precedes the 09:00 seed visit (14:00Z); Summary 'Your next visit' shows the 08:00 visit.
actual: AppStore.visits sorts with `$0.date < $1.date` on the raw strings. '2026-09-15T09:00:00-05:00' < '2026-09-15T13:00:00Z' lexicographically, so the later seed visit sorts first; SummaryView.nextVisit (SummaryView.swift:20) picks the first upcoming visit in that order and VisitsView (VisitsView.swift:17-19,34) lists them in that order. The same mismatch occurs for any two visits whose instants fall within the offset window (up to ~5 h for -05:00) around a day boundary, and for browser-created visits pulled from the server (Z format) against untouched seed visits.
impact: Wrong 'next visit' on the home screen and wrong Upcoming/Past ordering whenever visit dates mix time-zone offset and Z formats. The records sort (AppStore.swift:90-96) already parses dates, so this is an inconsistency inside one file. ReportEngine.signature and RevaDate.display parse correctly, so no report/staleness corruption; ordering only.
evidence: Source: AppStore.swift:98 string sort; seed.json:286,306,326 use '-05:00' offsets; VisitEditorView.swift:109 writes RevaDate.iso(date); Models.swift:217 ISO8601DateFormatter().string(from:) emits 'Z' UTC. Refutation attempt: checked whether AppStore.init or AppSnapshot.validate normalizes visit dates on load (they do not; AppStore.swift:54-87, Models.swift:169-186) and whether the editor rewrites untouched seed visits (only when a seed visit is edited and saved). Browser parity: apps/web/src/features/visits/VisitsPage.tsx:28-35 sorts by parsed epoch, so the browser orders the same data correctly. Runtime unverified (no simulator permitted); a pure-Swift string-comparison demonstration is requested as ER-04-03. | Independent validation: State/AppStore.swift:98; Features/Shared/SummaryView.swift:20; VisitsView.swift:17-34; RevaDate.iso; seed dates. evidence/codex-takeover/provider-context-repro.txt (compiler exit0, run exit0); evidence/codex-takeover/ProviderContextRepro.swift:73-108 uses production ReportEngine/AppStore/LocalRepository with synthetic data and a controlled transport double.
smallestFix: Sort by `RevaDate.parse($0.date) < RevaDate.parse($1.date)` (tie-break on id), matching the records sort in the same file; optionally normalize visit.date to RevaDate.iso on load or in the seed.
regressionCheck: Unit test in RevaCoreTests (or a new AppStore test target) constructing visits with '2026-09-15T09:00:00-05:00' and '2026-09-15T13:00:00Z' and asserting the Z visit sorts first; snapshot-level check that Summary next visit equals min-by-instant upcoming visit.
validatorDisposition: Confirmed and reproduced through production store.visits: 08:45Z is ordered before10:00+02:00 (08:00Z), while production parser proves the latter is earlier. Summary picks first upcoming by source. Synthetic state harness is real production-state execution, not a simulator/UI test.

title: Global error alert lives on RootView beneath modal sheets; failures raised while Settings or an editor sheet is open may never be shown
trigger: Open Medical profile > Settings (a .sheet, MedicalProfileView.swift:86), enter an unreachable Server URL (e.g. a closed loopback port) and tap 'Check available services' (SettingsView.swift:27) or 'Check connection'/'Push local snapshot' (SettingsView.swift:56-67). Equivalent paths: any failing store.perform save inside RecordEditorView.swift:75, VisitEditorView.swift:117, MedicalProfileEditor.swift:117, ReportEditorView.swift:40, AddRecordView.swift:265-281 (all presented as sheets).
expected: The error is presented to the user while the sheet is still open, or inline in the sheet, and the sheet stays open so they can correct the input.
actual: checkProviders (AppStore+Providers.swift:32) and sync (AppStore+Sync.swift:132) write store.errorMessage; the only presenter is the `.alert` attached to RootView's Group (RootView.swift:50-58), which sits under the presented sheet. SwiftUI presents that alert from the root hosting controller, which is already presenting the sheet; in that configuration the alert is commonly not shown (UIKit 'already presenting' refusal) until the sheet is dismissed, if at all. For 'Check available services' nothing else changes on screen (providerStatus stays nil = 'Not configured'), so the user sees the progress indicator vanish with no explanation. SymptomEntryEditorView avoids this by rendering its own inline error (SymptomEntryEditorView.swift:105-110,138), which indicates the pattern is known but not applied to the other sheets.
impact: Silent failures on the Settings connection/provider path and on rare save failures in five editor sheets. Data is not lost (saves fail atomically), but the user gets no feedback and may retry blindly or assume success.
evidence: Source proof of modifier placement: RootView.swift:50-58 (alert on root), MedicalProfileView.swift:86 (Settings sheet), SettingsView.swift:27,56-67 (actions), AppStore+Providers.swift:29-33 and AppStore+Sync.swift:130-134 (errorMessage writers), SymptomEntryEditorView.swift:105-110,133-139 (inline pattern). Features/Visits/RecordingSessionView.swift:55 (outside this track) writes store.errorMessage from a sheet too. Refutation attempt: looked for any per-sheet alert modifier or an overlay-window presenter in Features/** (none found by grep for '.alert(' outside RootView). The claim that the underlying alert does not surface is SwiftUI runtime behavior and could not be exercised here (no simulator permitted) — hence candidate, medium confidence; ER-04-02 requests the check. | Independent validation: Features/Shared/RootView.swift:50-58; MedicalProfileView Settings sheet; SettingsView actions; existing reviewer ER-04-02 remains unexecuted.
smallestFix: Attach the same errorMessage-bound `.alert` inside each sheet's NavigationStack content (or render inline errors as SymptomEntryEditorView does); for Settings, also surface provider/connection failures inline via serverStatus/providerStatus text.
regressionCheck: XCUITest: open Settings, set an unreachable URL, tap 'Check available services', assert an alert or inline error appears while the Settings sheet is still presented; repeat for a forced save failure in RecordEditorView (e.g., a repository stub that throws).
validatorDisposition: Root alert placement and missing sheet-local error presenters are confirmed source facts. Actual SwiftUI presentation behavior varies with view hierarchy/runtime; without the prohibited simulator experiment do not promote failed alert display to confirmed.
ownerTrack: Captain (shared RootView/error boundary); Person 1 for Records/Profile sheets; Person 2 for Visit/Report sheets

title: Visit editor time-zone picker shifts the already-entered wall-clock time, defaults to America/Chicago regardless of device zone, and offers only six zones; browser keeps wall-clock time and includes the device zone
trigger: On a device in America/New_York, open Add visit, set 'Date & time' to 10:00 (displayed in the default America/Chicago zone, VisitEditorView.swift:21,43-44), then change 'Time zone' to America/New_York and save.
expected: The appointment is 10:00 in the clinic's zone (New York), i.e. the entered wall-clock time is kept when the zone changes — which is what the browser editor does (apps/web/src/features/visits/VisitEditor.tsx:20,55-56 with visitDates.ts:31-44), and the default zone is the device zone.
actual: The DatePicker binds a Date instant (@State date) and the zone only changes the picker's display environment (VisitEditorView.swift:43-44); switching zones re-displays the same instant as 11:00 New York. If the user does not notice the shift, the saved visit (VisitEditorView.swift:109-110) is one hour off. The zone list is a fixed six-entry array (VisitEditorView.swift:47-50) with no device-zone entry; the default is the string 'America/Chicago' (line 21).
impact: Secondary-path appointment time errors for users outside the six listed zones or who set the time before the zone; native/browser behavior differs for the same action. DST arithmetic itself is correct (instant-based; display via RevaDate.display in the visit zone everywhere).
evidence: VisitEditorView.swift:20-21,43-52,99-117; Models.swift:217; browser VisitEditor.tsx:20,48-56 and visitDates.ts:16-44 (wall-clock components stored as a string until save). Refutation attempt: verified that no onChange(of: zone) handler re-derives the Date to preserve wall-clock components (none present) and that the default zone is not derived from TimeZone.current (it is a literal). | Independent validation: VisitEditorView.swift:20-21,43-51,109-110; browser VisitEditor.tsx:20,46-55.
smallestFix: On zone change, re-derive `date` so the calendar components stay constant in the new zone (as visitDates.ts does); default `zone` to TimeZone.current.identifier and include it in the Picker list (mirroring VisitEditor.tsx:125).
regressionCheck: Unit test on the conversion helper: entering 10:00 in Chicago then switching to New_York yields an instant displaying 10:00 New_York; UI test that the picker's displayed time is unchanged after a zone switch.
validatorDisposition: Time-zone changes preserve the Date instant and visibly alter wall time; that can be intentional date-picker semantics. The browser differs, defaults are not device-derived, and options are limited. Clarify policy/include local zone rather than asserting every zone change schedules the wrong time.

title: 'Create pre-visit brief' silently does nothing while a Gemini summary is in flight (connected AI on)
trigger: Turn on 'Use connected AI', save a document or symptom entry (AddRecordView.swift:277-279 / SymptomEntryEditorView.swift:136 start summarizeWithAI in the background, setting isProviderBusy), immediately open a visit and tap 'Create pre-visit brief'.
expected: Either the button is disabled while the provider is busy, or the tap yields a visible message ('A connected request is still running').
actual: The button is disabled only by the local `generating` flag (VisitDetailView.swift:76). prepare() (lines 165-171) calls generatePreferredReport, which returns false without setting errorMessage or notice when isProviderBusy is true (AppStore+AI.swift:36). The button shows a spinner for one run-loop turn and reverts; nothing else happens.
impact: Confusing no-op on the visit preparation path when connected AI is enabled; the user may assume preparation is broken. Local (non-AI) path is unaffected. title: Camera-scanned documents are saved as kind 'Notes', so the 'Scan' filter misses them; record kind is never user-editable
trigger: On a physical iPhone, Add record > 'Scan a document', capture pages, review, Save to Records. Then in Records choose the 'Scan' filter.
expected: A document produced by 'Scan a document' appears under 'Scan' (the intake row and the filter chip use the same word), or the kind can be corrected in the editor.
actual: DocumentScanner pages are rendered into a PDF (AddRecordView.swift:139-165) and ingested as mimeType 'application/pdf' (DocumentImportService.swift:288). AddRecordView assigns `kind: item.mimeType.hasPrefix("image") ? "Scan" : "Notes"` (line 268), so camera scans become 'Notes' with the generic doc.text symbol (Models.swift:47-57). Only photo-library images become 'Scan'. RecordEditorView has no kind field (RecordEditorView.swift:28-49), and 'Labs'/'Imaging'/'Procedure' kinds exist only in seed data.
impact: Filter incoherence for the most likely real-world intake path (camera); users cannot categorize their own uploads. Data is intact (originals, page mapping and OCR warnings are preserved), so this is a secondary-path categorization defect.
evidence: AddRecordView.swift:139-165,268; DocumentImportService.swift:288; RecordsView.swift:18-20 (filter list) and 22-28 (kind equality); RecordEditorView.swift:28-49; Models.swift:47-57. Refutation attempt: checked whether ImportedDocument carries a scan flag or whether AddRecordView tracks the scanner origin to set the kind (neither exists). | Independent validation: Device/DocumentScanner.swift:60; AddRecordView.swift:139-165,268; DocumentImportService.swift:287-289; RecordsView.swift:18-28.
smallestFix: Track intake origin in AddRecordView (a `scanned` flag set in the scanner onFinish path) and use it for the kind; add a kind Picker (Notes/Labs/Imaging/Procedure/Scan) to AddRecordView's review card and RecordEditorView.
regressionCheck: Unit-level: a scanner-origin ImportedDocument saved through the intake path yields kind == 'Scan'; UI: after a camera scan the 'Scan' filter lists the record.
validatorDisposition: Scanner callback generates application/pdf and AddRecordView assigns every non-image import Notes. The exact-kind Scan filter therefore cannot find a camera-scanned PDF. Source proof does not require asserting hardware scan quality.

title: Accessibility robustness: fixed-size badges with scaled text, fixed point sizes on Welcome, a 17pt dismiss target, notices/inline errors not announced, unused symptom auto-focus, decorative chevrons/share icon without explicit labels
trigger: Run with Larger Accessibility Sizes (AX3-AX5) and VoiceOver on Summary, Medical profile, a visit brief and the symptom editor.
expected: Text scales without clipping; controls have >= 44pt targets; status/error text is announced; decorative icons are hidden from VoiceOver; intended auto-focus works.
actual: (a) SummaryView.swift:137-139 initials in a fixed 36x36 frame with scaled caption text; MedicalProfileView.swift:26-29 initials in a fixed 60x60 frame with title2; ReportView.swift:55-56 question numbers in a fixed 24x24 circle; ViewComponents.swift:79 IconTile 42x42 with title3 symbol — at AX sizes text/symbols exceed the frames. (b) WelcomeView.swift:18,20 use fixed .system(size: 64/48) which do not scale with Dynamic Type. (c) SummaryView.swift:34-38 dismiss control is a bare 17pt symbol with no minimum frame. (d) SummaryView.swift:30-40 notice banner and SymptomEntryEditorView.swift:105-110 inline error are plain Text with no announcement or status trait. (e) SymptomEntryEditorView.swift:20,48 declares @FocusState symptomFocused and binds it but never sets it, so the intended auto-focus does not happen. (f) RecordRow.swift:28-29, VisitRow.swift:22 chevrons and SourcePreview.swift:32 image-only ShareLink label carry no explicit accessibility label/hidden trait. Positive: filter chips set .isSelected (RecordsView.swift:53), image-only toolbar buttons are labeled (RecordsView.swift:84, VisitsView.swift:57, MedicalProfileView.swift:83, SummaryView.swift:38,140), IconTile is accessibilityHidden, symptom fields carry labels.
impact: Cosmetic clipping and weaker screen-reader feedback at accessibility sizes; no functional block. Runtime unverified (no simulator permitted).
evidence: Line citations above, each verified with sed. Refutation attempt: checked for @ScaledMetric or minimumScaleFactor on the fixed frames (none) and for UIAccessibility.post/accessibilityAddTraits(.updatesFrequently) on notices (none). | Independent validation: SummaryView.swift:34-38,137-139; ReportView.swift:55-56; supervisor no-simulator rule and runner nativeUI exclusion.
smallestFix: Use @ScaledMetric for the badge frames or drop fixed sizes; replace fixed .system(size:) with text styles; give the dismiss button .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44); post UIAccessibility.announcement (or .accessibilityAddTraits(.updatesFrequently)) when notice/saveError change; set symptomFocused = true onAppear; add .accessibilityHidden(true) to chevrons and .accessibilityLabel("Share") to the ShareLink.
regressionCheck: Accessibility Inspector audit on Summary/Profile/Brief at AX5; VoiceOver pass confirming notice announcements.
validatorDisposition: The inventory mixes source-fixed sizes and missing explicit annotations with untested DynamicType/VoiceOver outcomes. System labels may be inferred and fixedframes need actual measurement before claiming clipping. Keep focused native accessibility checks, not a bundle of confirmed defects.

title: Visit-notes editor saves a stale whole VisitRecording and can erase a transcript that arrived while the sheet was open
trigger: On RecordingDetailView, tap 'Transcribe saved audio' (async, isProviderBusy does not disable 'Edit visit notes'), then open 'Edit visit notes' while transcription runs. Transcription completes and AppStore.transcribeRecording saves segments/transcriptionModel/status='transcribed' (AppStore+Transcription.swift:36-39). Tap Save in the notes sheet.
expected: Only VisitRecording.summary (the separate notes field) changes; the transcript segments, transcriptionModel and status saved a moment earlier remain (header contract: 'does not alter transcript words or audio').
actual: RecordingNotesEditor holds '@State var recording' initialised once from the sheet's initial value (line 15) and Save calls store.save(recording) (line 26); AppStore.save(_ recording:) replaces the whole element by id (AppStore+Recordings.swift:11-19). The stale draft (segments=[], transcriptionModel=nil, status='saved') overwrites the freshly saved transcript. The 'Transcribe saved audio' button is disabled only while segments are non-empty (RecordingDetailView.swift:77-79), so the transcript can be regenerated only by paying for another provider call; if a memory existed it keeps the transcript text until the next 'Update memory', which then rebuilds it from notes only.
impact: Loss of a paid Whisper transcript on a realistic overlap (user takes notes while waiting for transcription). Same last-writer-wins shape would also drop a segments change arriving from a sync pull while the sheet is open.
evidence: Source: RecordingNotesEditor.swift:15,26 (sed -n verified); AppStore+Recordings.swift:11-19 whole-object replace; RecordingDetailView.swift:74-80 (transcribe Task) and :127-128 ('Edit visit notes' not disabled during isProviderBusy) and :140-142 (sheet content re-evaluated but @State initial value is not reapplied); AppStore+Transcription.swift:18-20 shows the transcription path itself re-reads 'latest' before saving, i.e. the store already models this overlap as possible. Refutation attempt: checked whether SwiftUI recreates the editor state when the parent's 'recording' changes; State(initialValue:) applies only on first identity creation, so the draft stays stale. Contrast: TranscriptTextEditor + saveMemory guard Set(ids) == Set(keys) and reject a changed transcript (AppStore+Recordings.swift:49-55); the notes path has no equivalent guard. | Independent validation: RecordingNotesEditor.swift:15,19-26; State/AppStore+Recordings.swift:11-18; RecordingDetailView transcribe and note-edit controls; AppStore+Transcription latest publication.
smallestFix: Save notes through a field-targeted mutation, e.g. AppStore.updateRecordingNotes(id:summary:) that mutates only data.recordings[i].summary inside mutate; RecordingNotesEditor keeps only the recording ID plus a String draft. Optionally also disable 'Edit visit notes' while isProviderBusy.

title: A failed finish() leaves the recorder in a dead-end paused state whose only guidance is contradictory
trigger: finish() throws after stopping the recorder: verification fails because the file is empty/shorter than 0.1 s (Start then Finish within ~100 ms, or an input that produced no encoded frames), or AVAudioPlayer(contentsOf:) rejects a file left unfinalised after mediaServicesWereReset/encode error (both paths already set reachedEnd = true and tell the user to 'Save what was captured').
expected: Either the capture stays resumable so the user can 'record a little longer' as the emptyRecording message advises, or the recorder moves to an explicit terminal state with a single accurate instruction (discard and start again).
actual: finish() stops the AVAudioRecorder, sets isPaused = true and reachedEnd = true and releases the session before verification (lines 205-211); on failure it only sets errorMessage and rethrows (224-227), leaving isRecording == true and recorder != nil. The view then shows 'Paused' with Resume/Finish buttons. resume() hits 'guard !reachedEnd' and reports 'The one-hour recording limit was reached. Save this recording before starting another.' (lines 178-182) even though no time limit was reached; Finish repeats the same failure; start() throws .busy (line 111). The only exit is Close -> 'Discard recording'.
impact: Contradictory, incorrect user guidance on the failure path of the main recording flow (message says record longer; resume says one-hour limit reached; discard is the only way out). No data loss beyond the already-unusable draft.
evidence: Source lines verified with sed -n: AudioServices.swift:26 (emptyRecording text), :176-182 (resume guard and one-hour text), :202-228 (finish state changes before verification, catch does not reset state), :111 (start busy guard). RecordingSessionView.swift:42-46 renders Resume/Finish while isRecording. Refutation attempt: looked for any path that clears reachedEnd or recorder after a failed finish; only cancel()/cleanUpDraft() do (lines 232-253), which delete the draft. | Independent validation: Device/AudioServices.swift:176-182,202-227,232-252; RecordingSessionView.swift:42-46,77-89.
smallestFix: In finish()'s catch, transition to an explicit terminal state (e.g. a 'finishFailed' flag) and have resume() report 'This recording could not be finalised; discard it and start a new recording'; change the emptyRecording text to match (do not promise 'record a little longer'). Alternatively perform verification before setting reachedEnd and only mark terminal when the stop actually happened.
regressionCheck: Unit-style harness on AudioRecorder with an injected empty draft: after finish() throws, assert resume() publishes the finalisation message (not the one-hour text) and that cancel() returns to the ready state; UI check that the session screen offers a discard/restart action.
validatorDisposition: After verification throws, reachedEnd/isPaused remain true and isRecording remains true. Resume refuses reachedEnd with a one-hour message; repeated Finish repeats verification. This is a concrete error-state dead end until explicit discard. Triggered invalid-file/too-short case not run on hardware by validator.

title: Camera scan path allows 30 pages but assembles full-resolution pages into a PDF on the main actor and then applies the 16 MiB byte cap with a message that does not fit the camera path
trigger: On a physical iPhone, scan several pages with 'Scan a document' (VNDocumentCameraViewController) and tap Save in the scanner.
expected: A multi-page camera scan within the advertised page limit imports successfully, or is rejected with a message that tells the user what to do on this path (fewer pages); memory use is bounded by downsampling before PDF assembly.
actual: DocumentScanner accepts up to DocumentImportService.maximumPages (30) and materialises every page image at once (line 56-60). AddRecordView draws each full-resolution UIImage into a UIGraphicsPDFRenderer inside a MainActor Task (AddRecordView.swift:143-165), writes the PDF to tmp and calls ingest(url:), which rejects anything over 16 MiB with 'This file exceeds the 16 MB import limit. Export a smaller copy and try again.' (DocumentImportService.swift:47-48,120,131). Nothing downsamples scan pages (OCR downsampling at 2600 px happens only after the bytes are accepted). Camera page images are several megapixels each; Core Graphics embeds non-JPEG-backed bitmaps with Flate, so a handful of pages can exceed the cap while the page limit still says 30.
impact: Multi-page camera scans on hardware are likely rejected well below the advertised page limit with unactionable guidance, after a main-thread PDF assembly whose peak memory scales with page count x full-resolution bitmap size (concrete resource argument: N pages x W x H x 4 bytes held simultaneously plus the Flate-encoded PDF Data). Exact page count at which rejection occurs is unmeasured (hardware check unavailable to this audit).
evidence: Source: DocumentScanner.swift:52-60 (page limit and eager image materialisation), AddRecordView.swift:143-165 (full-size draw, main-actor Task), DocumentImportService.swift:70,117-135 (16 MiB stream bound), :47-48 (message). title: Server originals are never pruned and every referenced original is re-uploaded on each push; owner quota can be exhausted with no browser remedy
trigger: Over the life of one owner token, import and later delete records (or record a few audio memories and delete them), pushing after each change; or let several conflicting (409) pushes upload originals. Each push re-sends every original still referenced by the snapshot; originals of deleted records, and originals uploaded by a push whose CAS later failed, stay on the server forever.
expected: A push transfers only originals the server lacks, and the client (or server) has a path to remove originals no snapshot references, so the documented owner cap (128 files / 64 MiB, server Models.swift:126-128) is not consumed by orphans.
actual: store.ts:520-524 iterates originals(snapshot) and calls api.uploadAttachment for every one on every push (no existence check, no hash comparison). api.ts:249-252 implements deleteAttachment and api.ts:224-226 deleteState, but store.ts never calls either and APITransport (store.ts:23-36) does not expose them; native AppStore has no deleteAttachment/deleteState callers either (grep over apps/ios/Reva). Server putAttachment counts all owner attachments toward the cap including orphans (LocalFileStore.swift:110-121; PostgresStore.swift:120). With the checked-in seed, every push re-sends 9 originals / 618,312 bytes (fixture-manifest.json + seed.json) even when unchanged.
impact: Bandwidth: O(total referenced original bytes) per push, up to the 64 MiB owner cap per push. Robustness: once 128 distinct filenames have ever been uploaded for an owner (deleted-record originals and failed-CAS uploads included), every further push fails with HTTP 413 'Owner attachment limit is 64 MiB and 128 files' and the browser offers no pruning or reset path; only a native or manual DELETE /v1/state (which also destroys the snapshot) recovers.
evidence: Source proof: store.ts:520-524 (upload loop), store.ts:23-36 (APITransport lacks delete operations), api.ts:224-226 and 249-252 (unused delete methods), server/Sources/RevaServer/LocalFileStore.swift:110-121 (quota counts orphans), server/Sources/RevaServer/Models.swift:126-128 (caps). title: Persistence module depends on the transport module, and features bypass the injected store persistence through module-level attachment helpers
trigger: Inspect imports: repository.ts:7 imports boundedBytes, MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES and MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES from api.ts; repository.ts:287-290 exports a module singleton plus saveAttachment/getAttachment wrappers that ImportDialog.tsx:126, RecordingCapture.tsx:114, SourcePreview.tsx:34 and RecordingDetail.tsx:31 import directly.

impact: Maintainability/testability only: no runtime defect found. The store contract ('Injectable persistence contract keeps React independent of browser storage internals', repository.ts:9) is not fully honoured.

title: Attachment PUT/GET share the generic 25 s total deadline while a same-size transcription upload gets 110 s; large originals on slow links cannot be pushed or pulled
trigger: Push or pull a 16 MiB original (the documented cap) over a link slower than about 5.4 Mbit/s sustained (16 MiB / 25 s); the AbortController at api.ts:146-147 fires, send() throws the timeout error, and pushToServer/pullFromServer abort.
expected: Attachment transfers use a deadline proportional to size or an idle timeout, consistent with the 110 s allowed for the identical 16 MiB body in transcribe() (api.ts:302-303).
actual: uploadAttachment (api.ts:232-235) and attachment (api.ts:239-245) call send() with the default timeout = 25_000; because pushToServer re-uploads every original each attempt (store.ts:520-524), the same large file times out on every retry, so the workspace can never be pushed from that connection.
impact: Robustness on a secondary path; data is preserved (message says so) and the fixed deadline is a deliberate bound, hence a suggestion, not a defect. The 25 s cap also bounds each of up to 128 sequential downloads in a pull.
evidence: sed -n '138,172p;229,252p;294,304p' apps/web/src/core/api.ts. Arithmetic: 16 MiB = 134.2 Mbit; 134.2 / 25 s = 5.37 Mbit/s minimum. Native ServerClient uses URLSession timeoutInterval = 20 (apps/ios/Reva/Core/ServerClient.swift:100), which is an idle timeout, not a total deadline. | Independent validation: core/api.ts send default and uploadAttachment:232; store upload loop; original finding arithmetic16MiB/25s.
smallestFix: Pass a size-derived timeout for attachment transfers (for example max(25 s, bytes / 256 KiB per s)) or the same 110 s used for transcription.
regressionCheck: api.test: uploadAttachment with a 16 MiB Blob and a fetch mock that resolves after 30 s (fake timers) succeeds; a stalled fetch beyond the scaled deadline still rejects with the timeout message.
validatorDisposition: 25-second total transfer cap can reject large files on slow links; finite deadlines are deliberate and errors preserve data. Arithmetic is sufficient for a configuration tradeoff, not a measured user failure. Size-aware deadlines remain bounded and optional.

title: Forward-looking (accounts WIP): after an identity change the first connection check adopts the remote revision unconditionally, so the next push replaces that identity's server snapshot with the local (possibly demo) workspace
trigger: setToken('other-token') (store.ts:182-193 sets serverRevision null, mustPull false); checkServer (store.ts:486-509) reads the remote revision, and because known === null it publishes serverRevision = remote and reports 'Provider availability checked.' with no indication that the server holds a different snapshot; pushToServer (store.ts:510-540) then PUTs the local workspace with that base revision and succeeds.
expected: With static tokens the current UI copy ('Replace the server's snapshot with this browser's records and profile', SettingsPage.tsx:95-98) makes this explicit, so this is not a defect today. Under the accounts contract (per-user login into the same browser) a fresh login must not be able to overwrite an existing account snapshot with the demo or another user's workspace after a single check.
actual: The store has no notion of 'this browser has never pulled this identity's snapshot'; mustPull is only set by a 409 or by a revision change between checks (store.ts:502-508). The local IndexedDB name is fixed ('reva-workspace-v1', repository.ts:59) regardless of token.
impact: Integration risk for the concurrent accounts work (contract docs/task-specs/accounts-and-tiger.md: per-user IndexedDB DB name and 1.5 s debounced auto-push). If auto-push reuses pushToServer after login without a required pull, a demo workspace could be pushed into a real account (G06). Not a completed-path defect in this snapshot.

smallestFix: Track per-identity 'pulled or pushed at least once' in memory; when the first check after an identity change finds a non-tombstone remote snapshot, set mustPull (or require an explicit 'replace server copy' confirmation) before allowing push. Under accounts, bind the local DB name to the user id as the contract already specifies.
regressionCheck: Store test: setToken to a new identity whose pull returns revision 5 with a snapshot; checkServer; expect pushToServer to reject with the pull-first message until pullFromServer succeeds.
validatorDisposition: Static-token manual Replace-server workflow explicitly permits replacement; the concern is future automatic account login/upload, absent here. title: Browser pull overwrites a same-name local original without comparing bytes, unlike the native staging guard

actual: write() puts every downloaded Blob under its filename unconditionally (repository.ts:147) inside the same transaction that replaces the snapshot; the prior local bytes are gone after commit.
impact: Low: the replaced snapshot and its originals stay mutually consistent (both come from the server) and the user confirmed 'Pull and replace' (SettingsPage.tsx:210-213). title: Failed browser import saves leave unused attachment keys and retries allocate new keys
trigger: In an open import dialog, make the snapshot save fail after the original transaction succeeds, for example by allowing another tab to advance IndexedDB CAS. Click Save to Records again without reloading.
expected: A failed record save retains its chosen file for retry without creating another stored original per retry; preferably original and snapshot are one atomic commit or use a stable staged filename with rollback.
actual: Each save call generates a fresh UUID filename, awaits a separate saveAttachment transaction, and only afterwards calls saveRecord. The catch keeps the dialog open but neither removes the saved original nor reuses its filename. Every failed retry can add another attachment key with no record reference.
impact: Failed snapshot CAS can leave unreferenced original keys; retries allocate new keys. Snapshot consistency is preserved. Physical byte duplication and quota exhaustion were not measured.
evidence: ImportDialog.tsx:124-147 creates filename and persists original before saveRecord; 152-157 has error handling but no cleanup. repository.ts:177-185 commits attachments in a standalone transaction. core/store.ts:203-204 delegates record saving to a separate snapshot edit. Trigger: original save succeeds, record publication fails after another tab advances CAS, then retry in the same dialog. Impact: another unreachable original key per failed attempt.
smallestFix: Publish the original and record in the existing aggregate IndexedDB transaction, or retain one staged original identity across retries and remove that staging write on abandoned/failed publication. Keep the original selected in the dialog after an error.
regressionCheck: Use two repositories/tabs to induce stale CAS after import opens; fail and retry three times, assert no extra unreferenced attachment keys appear and the preexisting snapshot remains unchanged. validatorDisposition: Retain as targeted transport hardening. FoundationNetworking Gemini and shared voice transport collect Data before enforcing their decode caps, while the Apple Gemini path streams with a bound. The code and comments disclose this distinction. A fixed provider or proxy returning too much data can exceed the nominal cap in memory, but no oversized transport run, process failure or arbitrary-destination exploit was demonstrated.
title: Provider response limits are post-collection on Linux and in the shared voice transport
trigger: The fixed provider returns a response larger than the supported 1 MiB Gemini or 4 MiB voice JSON limit.
expected: If those values are intended as memory budgets, collection should stop as soon as the budget is exceeded.
actual: FoundationNetworking Gemini calls session.data before checking data.count; VoiceHTTPTransport does the same on every platform and VoiceProviderLimits checks later. Thus retained response memory is O(provider response bytes), not O(the configured byte cap). Apple Gemini uses bounded streaming correctly.
impact: A provider/proxy fault can consume more memory than the declared decoding limit before rejection. Fixed destinations and finite transport timeouts reduce exposure; no oversized live reply or process memory failure was observed. This is targeted hardening rather than a reproduced outage.
evidence: GeminiTransport.swift:38-48; VoiceTransport.swift:25-36,81-92. The file headers already disclose post-collection bounds. Current runner executes mocked service responses, not a streaming transport memory test. | Independent validation: Frozen server/Sources/RevaServer/Providers/GeminiTransport.swift:38-48; server/Sources/RevaServer/Providers/VoiceTransport.swift:25-36,81-92. smallestFix: Use a URLSessionDataDelegate or equivalent incremental collector with cancellation once the byte budget is crossed for FoundationNetworking and voice; retain redirect refusal and timeouts.
regressionCheck: Synthetic transport test streams cap+1 bytes then more; assert cancellation occurs at the bound and the failure is sanitized, without connecting to a live provider.

title: Durable call receipts live only under a local directory (default relative .local-data) even in PostgreSQL mode; an ephemeral or relocated data directory silently drops duplicate-call protection and uncertain-call visibility (forward-looking: Docker/Tiger WIP)
trigger: Run RevaAPI with REVA_ENABLE_LIVE_CALLS=true on a host whose filesystem does not survive a redeploy (container image without a mounted volume), or start the process from a different working directory without REVA_DATA_DIRECTORY (Configuration.swift:41 defaults to the relative path .local-data); then a client re-sends a requestID that was dialed before the redeploy, or polls it.
expected: The documented guarantee (VoiceCalls.swift:4-5, 92-94; evidence/context/reva-stack-spec.md:134) that intent/receipts survive restarts and redeploys, or a startup refusal to enable live calls without a verified persistent directory.
actual: ensureDirectory (VoiceCalls.swift:284-298) lazily creates a fresh empty voice-call-receipts tree wherever the directory resolves; read (305-308) returns nil for the earlier requestID, so start writes a new intent and dials again; details returns 404 for the earlier call. No receipt table exists in PostgresStore.swift (grep 'receipt' finds nothing) and nothing validates REVA_DATA_DIRECTORY at startup when live calls are enabled.
impact: The never-redial property holds only within one filesystem lifetime. Exposure today is bounded: the native UI has no same-requestID resubmission path (LiveBookingEditorView.swift:80-84 creates a new BookingRequest each time) and the browser store refuses to re-submit an existing local request (apps/web/src/core/store.ts:415). The risk materializes with the concurrent Dockerfile/Tiger deployment work if the data directory is not a persistent volume.
evidence: Source: VoiceCalls.swift:109-113 (directory derived from configuration.directory), 284-298, 305-308, 330-369; Configuration.swift:41; spec evidence/context/reva-stack-spec.md:134; delta patch line 237 documents 'preserve them across redeploys'. Refutation attempts: searched PostgresStore.swift/LocalFileStore.swift/HTTP.swift for receipt persistence (none); searched both clients for same-requestID resubmission (none). Documented tradeoff, hence suggestion rather than defect. | Independent validation: Frozen server/Sources/RevaServer/Providers/VoiceCalls.swift:109-113,129-145,284-308; server/Sources/RevaServer/Configuration.swift:41; server/README.md:98,100; apps/ios/Reva/Features/Visits/LiveBookingEditorView.swift:80-84; apps/web/src/core/store.ts:415. Trigger: operator discards or relocates receipt storage, then an external client resubmits the prior ID.
smallestFix: Carry the existing persistent-volume requirement for call receipts into completed deployment configuration and verify receipts survive process recreation and redeploy. An absolute-path policy is optional hardening and does not itself establish durability.
regressionCheck: Persist a synthetic uncertain/completed call receipt, recreate the deployed process or container using its configured persistent volume, then replay/poll the same owner/request and assert no new dial. Use a fake provider; do not place a real call for this test.
validatorDisposition: Retain as a deployment-hardening suggestion and lower its priority from P2 to P3. File receipts are deliberately separate from PostgreSQL snapshots; the frozen server README explicitly requires persistent storage and preservation across redeploys. Losing that storage can lose duplicate-call protection if an external client later resubmits the old request ID, but neither current UI resubmits an existing request. Ephemeral Docker/Tiger deployment was unfinished and is not evidence of a delivered-path defect. Requiring an absolute directory alone would not prove persistence.

actual: Only predev and prebuild run assets. Tests import ignored public/demo/seed.json and expected-evidence.json, so clean typecheck fails with missing module/type errors and Vitest fails five files. The runner then ran the normal build (which generates assets), and both checks passed.
impact: Clean CI/contributor verification fails even though production build succeeds. Warm working directories conceal the prerequisite and can produce misleading readiness reports.
evidence: Reproduced by runner: evidence/r1-06-typecheck.log (TS2307 and dependent errors), evidence/r1-07-vitest.log (5 failed files, 2 passed), then r1-06b-typecheck-after-assets.log and r1-07b-vitest-after-assets.log (77 passed). Source: package.json:10-17; src/core/__tests__/fixtures.ts:5; src/core/__tests__/domain.test.ts:6; .gitignore generated public/demo exclusion. No Codex rerun is claimed. | Independent validation: evidence/r1-06-typecheck.log exit1; r1-07-vitest.log5failedfiles; r1-06b-typecheck-after-assets.log exit0; r1-07b-vitest-after-assets.log77passed; package.json:10-17.
smallestFix: Have typecheck/test prepare their required fixtures, or import checked-in native fixture sources through a deliberate test fixture boundary. Update the clean integration command sequence so it cannot skip required generation.
regressionCheck: In a clean isolated checkout with public/demo absent, npm ci followed by the documented typecheck/test sequence succeeds; production build still includes byte-identical fictional originals and local OCR assets.
validatorDisposition: Independent reading of saved failing/passing logs confirms a reproducible clean checkout prerequisite defect. Production build correctly runs prebuild; only standalone typecheck/test command readiness is affected.
